findings.title: Feature-disabled gating is only tested for metadata and its exit code is not asserted
findings.body: The new test covers only `update-compatibility metadata` without `--features=rolling-updates` and only asserts the error message. It does not cover the separately added gating in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and does not assert exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`) for either subcommand. A regression that leaves `check` ungated, or returns the picocli software/usage error codes instead of 4, would therefore pass while breaking scripts and the operator flow that rely on distinguishing feature-disabled from recreate (3) and rolling (0).

findings.title: Caution overstates that the operator will fail without rolling-updates
findings.body: The new caution says that while in preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. That is not scoped to using `spec.update.strategy`, and it contradicts the PR's own operator test setup in UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment, where the default/null-strategy deployment returns before enabling `rolling-updates` and is still expected to deploy and upgrade. As written, users with ordinary CRs will believe every deployment must enable a preview feature or the operator fails; the text should be limited to deployments that use the update-strategy feature.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is described as a compatibility verdict although no check ran
findings.body: The table describes exit code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' when the feature is disabled. In that case UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata return before validating/reading metadata or computing compatibility, so compatibility is unknown rather than disproven. Scripts following this wording may permanently choose a recreate/downtime path for a merely misconfigured invocation instead of treating 4 as an enablement/configuration error distinct from the recreate verdict (3).
